points.description: Correct construction of D (e.g. as the appropriate isogonal conjugate-type point of A with respect to the angle/quadrilateral YBAC, D ≠ A and inside angle XYZ), with a justification that it exists and differs from A. Equivalent constructions are acceptable.

levels.says: Gives a candidate D but existence, D≠A, or being inside the angle is not justified.

points.description: Identifies and proves the necessary and sufficient condition for the isogonal conjugate of a point to exist in quadrilateral YBAC (e.g. angle-sum condition on opposite angles / equal angle pairs at B and C), and shows this holds for every admissible B, C when ∠BAC = ∠XYZ, using ∠XYZ ≠ 60° where needed.

levels.says: States the condition but does not fully prove it or does not show it applies for all B, C.

points.description: Shows that the same D works for all B, C on the rays with ∠BAC = ∠XYZ (D is independent of B and C), via the angle relations of the isogonal pair in the quadrilateral.
Computes θ correctly as a constant in (0, 2π) in terms of ∠XYZ (e.g. from ∠BDC = angle relation with ∠BAC and ∠XYZ), and concludes ∠BDC = θ.

rubric.notes: Full marks need a valid construction of D, justification of the isogonal-conjugate condition, independence of B and C, and the correct constant θ. Minor verification slips lose small marks only. Equivalent methods (e.g. coordinates or inversion) earn equivalent credit.
